Header: Mus musculus, Rattus rattus, Arvicanthus niloticus

Prevention: Remove weeds, heavy mulches, and dense vegetative cover which provide rodents food and protection from predators and environmental stresses.
Use weed-free strips to serve as buffers around areas requiring protection.
Wire fences at least 12 inches above ground with a mesh size of 1/4 inch or smaller will help to exclude voles from the field
Put metal guards around stands of storage structures to prevent rodents from climbing and entering stores
Monitoring: Additional relevant crops: maize, rice, sorghum, yam, cassava, sweet potato
Be alert for the presence of rats and mice both in production field and during storage.
Look for fresh trails in the grass, burrows, droppings, furs and evidence of feeding in the field and stores
Pay particular attention to adjacent areas that have heavy vegetation, because such areas are likely sources of invasions.
Frequently check protective devices to make sure meadow mice haven’t gnawed through or dug beneath the cylinders and are hiding inside the tree guard while they feed on the tree.
Take action when evidence of rodent presence as outlined above is clear
Direct Control: Trap and destroy rodents using locally made traps baited with peanut butter-fish meal mixture.
Place traps at right angles to runaways with the trigger end on the runaway.
Use predators such as dogs and cats to to reduce rodent population in the area
Rodents can also be killed by hunting using catapults, and bows and arrows
Restrictions: Rodenticides are available but are classed as highly hazardous by
WHO and so are not recommended here.
